headline: UK inflation rises to one-year high of 3.6% in October
summary: UK inflation reached a one-year high of 3.6% in October, driven by energy prices and tobacco taxes. Despite the headline increase, markets trimmed expectations for future interest rate hikes due to stable underlying measures.
why: Inflation data is a primary input for the Bank of England's monetary policy decisions, directly influencing interest rates and currency valuation.

impacts.name: UK 10-year Gilt yield
impacts.why: Lowered rate hike bets reduce yields.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Markets adjusted expectations for central bank policy based on underlying inflation components.
